14-4.title: Last Tile of the Wall
14-4.subtitle: 海底撈月 — winning on the final draw

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: 海底撈月 is the last-tile hand: you win on the very last tile drawn from the wall, and it is worth 1 faan.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: It is always a self-draw. That tile never came from anyone's discard, so 自摸 is inside the hand as well.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: So 自摸 and 海底 together already make 2 faan?

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Two, which is still short of the 3-faan minimum, so you need one more item before the hand is even legal.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: And if that last tile is thrown away instead, there is no 海底 at all. Somebody just wins normally on a discard.

questions.question: When exactly does 海底撈月 apply?
options: When you draw the final tile left in the wall and it completes your hand
When you win on the final discard of the hand
When you declare a kong on your last turn
When your hand contains only one suit
questions.explanation: 海底撈月 is defined by the source of the tile: the last tile in the wall, drawn by you, and it completes the hand.

questions.question: How many faan is 海底撈月 worth on its own?
questions.explanation: It sits in the 1-faan group, alongside 自摸 and 門前清, so it is a small bonus rather than a limit hand.

questions.question: The wall is empty, and the player to your left discards the tile that completes your hand. Do you score 海底撈月?
options: Yes, it is still the last tile of the hand
No, 海底撈月 needs a tile you drew yourself
Yes, but only if you also score 自摸
Yes, and the hand becomes a 10-faan limit
questions.explanation: A discarded final tile is an ordinary discard win. 海底撈月 only counts the last tile drawn from the wall, so a claimed tile never earns it.

questions.question: Which statements about 海底撈月 are correct?
options: It is a 1-faan item
It can stack with 自摸 for 2 faan
It can be won on another player's discard
It is one of the 10-faan limit hands
questions.explanation: It is 1 faan and it stacks with 自摸, because a last-tile win is always self-drawn. It is not a limit hand, and it cannot come from a discard.

questions.question: Match each winning situation to the faan item it earns.

pairs.left: Drawing the final tile of the wall to win
Winning on any tile you drew yourself
Winning on the tile a player adds to their kong
Winning on the replacement tile straight after your own kong

questions.explanation: All four are 1-faan items, and each is triggered by a different source of tile: the wall's last tile, any self-draw, a robbed kong tile, or a kong replacement.

questions.question: Adding 自摸 and 海底撈月 together gives how many faan?
questions.explanation: 1 faan for 自摸 plus 1 faan for 海底撈月 is 2, which on its own is still below the 3-faan minimum needed to win.

questions.question: Your hand is 平糊, won by 自摸 on the last tile of the wall, so 3 faan in total. What does each of the other three players pay?
options: 4 points
8 points
12 points
24 points
questions.explanation: A 3-faan hand is 8 from a discarder, and on a self-draw the other three each pay half of that, so 4 points each and 12 in total.

questions.question: The last tile of the wall is about to be drawn. Your hand holds {{p3}}{{p3}} and one more copy turns that pair into a pung. Which tile do you need?
options: p3
p4
p2
east
questions.explanation: A pair becomes a pung only with a third copy of the same tile, so {{p3}} is the only card that completes the set.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: 門前清 means a front hand: you never chowed, punged or made an exposed kong before you won. It is worth 1 faan.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: A concealed kong is the exception. Gary's ruling is that 暗槓 keeps 門前清, because nobody at the table supplied those tiles.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: So the real test is whether the other players saw me take a tile from someone else?

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: That is the whole test. One chow or pung and the 1 faan is gone for the rest of the hand, however clean you play afterwards.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: With 自摸 on top you reach 2 faan, still under the 3-faan minimum, so a concealed hand usually needs one more item to be worth declaring.

questions.question: How many faan is 門前清 worth?
questions.explanation: 門前清 is a 1-faan item, the same size as 自摸 and 海底撈月.

questions.question: Which of these actions destroys 門前清?
options: Declaring a concealed kong 暗槓
Claiming a discard to complete a chow
Drawing a flower tile
Winning on another player's discard
questions.explanation: Claiming a discard for a chow opens the hand. A concealed kong and flower draws do not, and neither does winning on a discard.

questions.question: You declared a concealed kong 暗槓 early in the hand, then won later. Do you still score 門前清?
options: Yes, a concealed kong does not break it
No, any kong breaks it
Only if you also win by self-draw
Only if the kong was a wind tile
questions.explanation: Gary's ruling is that 暗槓 keeps 門前清, because no other player gave you those tiles. Only an exposed kong 明槓 breaks the concealment.

questions.question: Which of these leave 門前清 intact?
options: Winning on a discarded tile
Declaring a concealed kong
Claiming a discard to pung
Chowing a discarded tile
questions.explanation: The winning discard is not a meld you made, and a concealed kong takes nothing from the table. Punging or chowing a discard turns the hand open and kills the 1 faan.

questions.question: Match each action to its effect on 門前清.

pairs.left: Declaring a concealed kong 暗槓
pairs.right: Kept, the tiles came from your own hand

pairs.left: Making an exposed kong 明槓
pairs.right: Lost, the meld was supplied by a discard

pairs.left: Claiming a discard for a chow or pung
pairs.right: Lost, the hand is now open
Kept, a winning discard is not a meld

questions.explanation: Concealment is broken by melds built from other players' tiles. A concealed kong and a winning discard both leave the hand closed.

questions.question: 門前清 plus 自摸 comes to how many faan?
questions.explanation: 1 faan for 門前清 plus 1 faan for 自摸 is 2, and the hand still needs a third faan to reach the 3-faan minimum.

questions.question: Your hand scores only 門前清 and 自摸, for 2 faan. What happens?
options: You may win, and each player pays 2 points
You cannot win yet, because 3 faan is the minimum
You may win, but only on a discard
You may win, and the hand is rounded up to 3 faan
questions.explanation: The table only starts at 3 faan, so a 2-faan hand is not payable. You keep building until a third item arrives.

questions.question: You hold {{p5}}{{p7}} and are still concealed. A discard of which tile would complete a chow and cost you 門前清?
options: p6
p5
p8
east
questions.explanation: {{p5}} and {{p7}} are a closed wait that only {{p6}} fills, so that is the discard that would open the hand.
